name: cl
rationale: Per L1, programming languages are themselves cards. CL is the *primary* language card in Pheros_Studio — the one the autonomous loop emits, the one card-to-code synthesis writes into, and the one all other languages are reachable from via emission. CL exists so that the substrate has a uniform source representation that survives target-language churn: when the studio wants to add Wasm or a quantum backend or a new hardware target, the existing CL programs need not change.
statement: CL (Card Language) is the substrate's first-class card-native language. A CL program is a typed expression whose atoms are references to cards under cards/computation/<cat>/<subcat>/<name>/. The compiler resolves these references to specific variants/transpositions at emit time and produces target code (Python, Rust, Lean, CUDA, QASM, etc.). New primitives, types, transpositions, and target languages are added as cards, not as compiler edits.
